title: Test Run
intro: HAB: Hi! I'm HAB, your [[habitat]] computer. This is a short test run.
HAB: Keep power, oxygen and food above zero for 7 [[sol|sols]].
HAB: Walk to a wall panel and press E to switch a system. Each one costs power every sol.
HAB: Sleep in the bed, or press N, to go to the next sol. Outside there are rock samples to collect.

abort.message: The battery ran empty. HAB did a safe abort and kept you safe.
Oxygen got low, so HAB did a safe abort. Life support needs power to make oxygen.
Food ran out, so HAB called a safe abort. Greenhouse lights grow food.
Your radiation dose reached the safe limit, so HAB called a safe abort.

events.hab: HAB: Look at the Power meter. With everything on, we use more power than the Sun gives.
HAB: A dust storm! The sky is getting dark. Less sun reaches our [[solar|solar panels]].
HAB: A very cold night. If the heater is off, frost forms and life support makes less [[oxygen]].
HAB: Alert! A solar storm! See the [[aurora]] in the sky? The red lamp means [[radiation]] is high.
HAB: Uh oh. The rover drove into [[softsand|soft sand]].

cards.prompt: Dust is cutting our power. What do we do?

options.label: Turn off the science lab
options.hab: Lab off. That saves power every sol.

options.label: Go outside and clean the panels
options.hab: Panels are clean! That was a lot of oxygen, though.

options.label: Ask Earth what to do
options.hab: Earth's answer took a whole sol to arrive. Earth says: turn off what you don't need.

options.label: Use procedure card: Low Power
options.hab: Procedure card: science lab and radio off. Done right away, no waiting.

cards.prompt: Solar storm! Radiation is 8 times higher for 2 sols.

options.label: Procedure card: walk to the shelter now
options.hab: Go! The shelter is outside, past the airlock. Its thick walls block most radiation. Stay there and sleep with N.

options.label: Put up shield panels in the habitat
options.hab: Shield panels are up. They help a little.

options.label: Keep working outside
options.hab: You found a rock sample, but your radiation dose went up a lot.

cards.prompt: The rover is stuck in soft sand. What now?

options.label: Drive out slowly, a little each sol
options.hab: Slow and steady. That's how Opportunity escaped Purgatory Dune in 2005.

options.label: Go out and dig the wheels free
options.hab: Hard work! The wheels are free, but digging used a lot of oxygen.

debrief.realTeam: Real Mars teams switch off anything they don't need when power is low, hide from solar storms behind thick walls, and free stuck rovers very slowly.
debrief.tryNext: Try Pilot difficulty and ignore every warning, to see a safe abort. Then try again and turn things off early.

realScience.title: Aurora on Mars
realScience.text: Mars has [[aurora|auroras]] too! When a solar storm hits, particles from the Sun make the sky glow. In 2024 the rover Perseverance took the first picture of an aurora from the ground on Mars.
